status: qualified native worker managed-allocation windows; GPU-owned scheduler lifetime profiles remain open
head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1

validation.initial_build_attempt: The sandbox blocked access to the user systemd bus before compilation. The authorized retry succeeded with the established resource caps; both logs are retained.

changes: The managed allocator tracks one bounded measurement window per serial worker job, including all live allocations at entry and every transient reservation.
Per-window counters do not reset cumulative peaks or alter allocation leases. Overlapping windows reject; dropped/aborted windows clean up only measurement state.

The CLI/native process worker emits structured job_drained and shutdown reports after its existing drains. The shutdown window outlives the engine accounting object without retaining device resources.

Small and full-size C-service tests check report PID against the observed service identity, continuity across idle boundaries, per-job/cumulative peaks, enforced caps, retained caches and complete managed allocation release.
No proof container, parameter, registry identity, activation or framed worker protocol changed.
limitations: These are allocator-managed reservation peaks, not whole-device physical VRAM, host RSS, or driver/context measurements.
Measurement windows and logs are diagnostics, not resource admission, proof verification, or worker termination authority.
The full-size jobs finalize the same terminal statement via different verified dependencies; these timings do not establish sustained transaction throughput or full block production.

Complete GPU-owned scheduler lifetime profiles and admission remain open. Adaptive LDE phases must reserve the enforced managed cap or impose a real tile bound; measured peaks do not prove a complete analytical lifetime bound.
Full-size merges with two nonempty children, broader transaction kinds and block sizes, sustained multi-GPU saturation, AMD and Metal still require qualification.
